Patient: I'm 58 years old and female. I'm here because I have this foot ulcer that just won't heal, and I'm worried about it. It's been going on for about a year now.
Doctor: Could you please provide more details about your diabetes status, including whether you have been diagnosed with diabetes, the type of diabetes, and how long you have had it? Additionally, have you had any history of infections or cardiovascular conditions?
Patient: I was diagnosed with type two diabetes a few years back, and my blood sugars have been running in the two hundreds, which my doctor doesn't like. My last A1C was about ten, so I know it's not well-controlled. I haven't had any major infections or heart issues that I'm aware of.
Doctor: Could you describe the location, size, appearance, and any associated symptoms (e.g., pain, drainage, odor) of the foot ulcer? Have you noticed any changes in its appearance over the past year?
Patient: It's on the top of my right foot, near the fifth toe, and it's about an inch in size. It's got some yellow stuff in it, and there's been more drainage lately. It doesn't hurt, but I don't feel much in my foot anyway. I've noticed it hasn't been getting better, and it seems to be getting more draining over time.
Doctor: Have you had any recent fever, chills, or signs of systemic infection such as malaise or weight loss? Have you had any prior wound cultures or imaging of the foot ulcer?
Patient: I haven't had any fever or chills, but I have been feeling more tired lately. As for imaging, I think they did an x-ray before I came in, and it showed no bone infection, if I remember right. I don't think they did a wound culture.
Doctor: Could you please describe the depth of the ulcer and whether there is any necrotic tissue present? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in the color or texture of the surrounding skin?
Patient: The ulcer isn't very deep as far as I can tell, and there's some yellow stuff in there, but I don't think there's any dead tissue exposed. The skin around it doesn't look red or swollen, and it doesn't feel different to the touch. It just looks kind of open and has that yellowish stuff in it.
Doctor: Has the patient had any prior episodes of foot ulcers or infections, and is she currently on any antibiotics or wound care regimen?
Patient: I don't think I've had any other foot ulcers before, just this one. I was on some antibiotics a while back, maybe five months ago, but I don't think I'm on anything now. I've been trying to take care of it, but nothing really seems to be working.
Doctor: Has the patient undergone any vascular studies, such as an ankle-brachial index (ABI) or Doppler ultrasound, to assess peripheral arterial disease?
Patient: No, I don't think I've had any vascular studies done before. I wasn't really aware that was something they would check for this kind of wound. I just thought it was a regular ulcer that wasn't healing.
Doctor: Could you please share more details about your current diabetes management, including any medications you are taking, your diet, and whether you have experienced any complications related to your diabetes?
Patient: My diabetes is still not great, my blood sugars are still running around two hundred, and my last A1c was about ten. I'm on insulin and metformin, but it's not where my doctor wants it to be. I try to eat better, but I know I'm not doing enough. I also don't take good care of my feet like I should, which is probably making this ulcer worse.

Patient: No, I don't think I've had any vascular studies done before. I wasn't really aware that was something they would check for this kind of wound. I just thought it was a regular ulcer that wasn't healing.

reference_so.subjective:
Basic information: 58-year-old female presenting with a non-healing foot ulcer for approximately one year.

History of present illness: The patient has a non-healing foot ulcer located on the top of her right foot, near the fifth toe, measuring approximately one inch in size. The ulcer has yellow drainage and increased drainage over time. The patient reports no pain but has diminished sensation in her foot. She has a history of type 2 diabetes with poorly controlled blood sugar levels, with recent blood glucose readings in the 200s and an A1C of approximately 10. She has not reported any major infections or cardiovascular issues. The ulcer is not very deep, and there is no necrotic tissue exposed. The surrounding skin is not erythematous or swollen. The patient reports fatigue but no fever or chills. She confirms no prior foot ulcers and no current antibiotic use. She states no erythema, warmth, or systemic signs of infection. She confirms no necrotic tissue exposed and no prior wound culture performed. Patient acknowledges lack of awareness regarding vascular studies for foot ulcers and poor diabetes management with suboptimal glycemic control (blood glucose in 200s, A1C ~10) and inadequate foot care.

Past history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, poorly controlled; prior antibiotic use five months ago, unspecified antibiotic; no vascular studies performed for peripheral arterial disease.
